$comment: WC-012 — WorkCaptain code <-> runtime environment contract.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The CSP/HSTS release (workcaptain:18) shipped correct HSTS code
and production still emitted no HSTS header. Nothing was broken: app/server.js gates HSTS
on isHttps(), which trusts the ALB's x-forwarded-proto ONLY when TRUSTED_PROXY is '1' or
'true' — and TRUSTED_PROXY was never present in the production task definition.
CI could not have caught it. tests/security/security_headers.test.js spawns the server with
TRUSTED_PROXY: '1' injected, so it proves the behaviour WHEN the variable is set. The test was
right. Production simply did not match the environment the test supplied. A green suite and a
broken production surface were both telling the truth about different environments.
This contract is the missing third artefact: it states, in machine-readable form, what the
shipped code REQUIRES of its runtime, so a release can be checked against the environment it
will actually run in rather than the one the tests construct.
CLASSES
REQUIRED_RUNTIME  - the application cannot behave correctly without it
BEHAVIOUR_GATING  - the application runs, but security/business behaviour changes silently
OPTIONAL_RUNTIME  - optional, with a safe explicit default in code
SECRET_RUNTIME    - supplied via task-definition secrets, never plaintext environment
BUILD_ONLY        - not required by the production runtime
TEST_ONLY         - not used by the production runtime
Secrets are named here as IDENTITIES only. No secret value appears in this file and none may.

variables.name: TRUSTED_PROXY
variables.read_location: app/server.js:211 (also gates clientIp at :286 and isHttps at :351)
variables.default_behaviour: absent => false => x-forwarded-proto is NOT trusted
variables.reason: Required for the ALB's x-forwarded-proto to be trusted. Without it isHttps() is always false behind the load balancer, so Strict-Transport-Security is never emitted, and clientIp() reports the ALB address instead of the real client.

variables.name: NODE_ENV
variables.default_behaviour: absent => development semantics in a production image
variables.reason: Selects production behaviour across the application, including config validation.

variables.name: PROWORK_DATA_DIR
variables.default_behaviour: absent => falls back to a development path inside the container
variables.reason: Production data root. A dev fallback in production writes to the wrong location.

variables.name: APP_PORT
variables.reason: Must agree with the task definition's containerPort and the target group port.

variables.name: PORT
variables.reason: Redundant with APP_PORT; currently supplied and consistent.

variables.name: CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
variables.default_behaviour: absent/empty => the allowlist is empty and applyCors permits any Origin
variables.reason: Empty allowlist disables origin enforcement rather than denying, so absence silently widens CORS.

variables.name: DATABASE_URL
variables.reason: Database connection string. Secret-backed identity only; never plaintext environment.

variables.name: ADMIN_API_TOKEN
variables.reason: Administrative API credential. Secret-backed identity only.

variables.name: JWT_SECRET
variables.reason: Token signing key. A stale-Terraform apply is known to strip this; it must be asserted present and secret-backed.

variables.name: HYPERPAY_MODE
variables.default_behaviour: not read by any application code
variables.reason: Supplied by the production task definition but read NOWHERE in the codebase (measured 2026-09-12). Recorded so it is not mistaken for the control that keeps payments disabled — it is not. Left in place deliberately: removing it is a production delta and belongs to WC-008, not here.
